rationale: The problem is flow through a pathway with many handoffs, which is what Lean value stream mapping and redesign address. Completion charted by index-case month cohorts gives stable subgroups of about 100 contacts (the retrieved methods paper), so change can be separated from noise within a year. Reporting follows SQUIRE 2.0.
alternatives: Randomised comparison of home and clinic testing (refused: one program, and home testing is already the best supported change)
PDSA cycles without mapping (refused: the handoff structure is the problem)
whyNotMoreComplex: A controlled study would need several health units; the program needs to fix its own flow and show it on its own data.

decision.statement: Map the contact pathway value stream and redesign it from January 2027 (home blood draw, results routed to the case nurse, X-ray booked at the result visit), because losses concentrate between test and radiograph (c1), a comparable Lean redesign raised 60-day completion (c2) and home testing is the best supported change (c3), charting completion by index-case month from a checked monthly extract (c4).
decision.question: Should the TB program redesign its contact pathway with Lean methods, and how should it measure the result?

criteria.text: Losses concentrate at handoffs that the redesign removes, and a comparable redesign improved completion.
Completion falls for contacts in shelters or needing interpreters after the redesign.

gates.requirement: Medical officer of health approval of the Lean project and mapping days
gates.evidence: Memo MOH-TB-2026-05 dated 2026-09-01, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Data steward approval of the monthly de-identified extract
gates.evidence: Approval DS-114 dated 2026-09-12, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Text reminders to contacts without redesign
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c4 from dated, rated records; the interpreter claim c5 from an unrated report is carried only in the defeating criterion. Both gates are met on investigator-supplied approvals.

summary: Lean redesign recommended; both gates met.
